_comment: How each trail is drawn (docs/plan/SKINS-PLAN.md, 'Trails: how it works'). A trail is ribbons (strips laid along the path just flown) plus pieces (small 3D models dropped behind, scattered round the path and tumbling). `life`: seconds a bit of trail lives, so the stream is as long as one second of flight. `width`: studs across at the plane's tail. `fast_growth`: how much bigger the trail gets, reached at `fast_at` times the build's own speed. `grow_in`: the share of its life a piece takes to grow to full size (pieces leave the tail small, so the ones passing under your own camera are still small). `hangar_length`: studs of trail shown on the still plane in the hangar. Ribbon: `picture` (assets/fx/trails/<name>.png, spanning the whole trail) and `width` (times the common width), or `strands` thin cords of `colors`, each `width` studs, wound `radius` studs round the path; `taper` and `fade` (start to end: width share, see-through share), `twist` (turns a second), `look` (foil). Piece: `model` (star, flake, shard, spark, puff, bolt: about 1 stud across; soft: a smoke card that faces the camera), `look` (foil: crinkled metal; matte: cotton; soft: smoke; glow: a light), `rate` (a second at the build's own speed; it rises with speed so the spacing stays even), `life` (seconds, least to most), `size` (studs at birth, smallest to biggest; more small ones than big), `shrink` (its size at the end, as a share: over 1 it swells like smoke), `vanish` (the last share of its life over which it fades out), `spread` (studs: how far from the path a piece can start), `drift` (studs a second, any direction), `rise` (studs a second squared, up), `spin` (degrees a second, about a random axis), `align` (lies along the flight path), `twinkle` (size flickers this many times a second), `flash` (lightning: on, off, on, gone), `light` (it lights what is round it, this strong), `rainbow` (its colour runs through `colors` along the stream; a number runs through them that many times over), `colors` (else one picked for each piece). In the game (src/client/PlaneTrails.luau): soft and spark pieces are Roblox particles using Roblox's own smoke and sparkle pictures; a flake is a plain thin block; the others are the uploaded models in `meshes` (tools/art/trail_pieces.py makes them; 0 = not uploaded yet, so that piece is not drawn).
